results.title: Lear, Bosch discuss playbook on navigating tariffs, supply-chain snags
results.content:
Lear Corp. CEO Ray Scott emphasizes localization, alternative designs and onshoring as available responses to supply-chain challenges like tariffs.

Executives from the companies this week spoke before the Automotive Press Association, sharing details on how the manufacturers are thinking about the challenges. [...] From the COVID-19 pandemic to President Donald Trump's tariffs on vehicles and their parts to halted exports of semiconductors out of China by manufacturer Nexperia, companies like Southfield-based Lear Corp., which makes seats and electronic systems, and Germany's Robert Bosch GmbH, which makes parts from brakes to electronic control units, say it's a daily battle to ensure the proper flow of parts needed to make the parts needed in the trucks, SUVs and cars Americans drive. [...] "I'm all for an ambitious goal to build more here in the U.S. and supply great jobs," Lear CEO Ray Scott said at the company's innovation center at its Southfield headquarters. "But if you think about the supply chain that's been built over 25 years, trying to do that overnight is very challenging. So staying focused on the goal, which I think is the right goal, but how you do it and when you do things is very important."

results.content:
## GaMEP Expertise

 Supply chain assessment: We evaluate your supply chain — from raw material to finished product — to identify risks and opportunities.
 Supplier scouting: We search for and connect you with qualified domestic suppliers.

 Process improvement: We apply lean practices to improve production and reduce costs.
 Technology automation: We analyze and help implement appropriate technologies. [...] Reshoring: Consider automation opportunities and domestic suppliers (including those who can expand their production).
 Nearshoring: Take advantage of duty-free imports through Mexico.
 Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States Chapter 98 and Chapter 99: Eliminate or reduce duties for qualifying products.
 Bonded warehouses: Store imported products while deferring duties until they leave the facility (quarterly harbor maintenance fees apply).
